text:
Marta V: Quick ask — we're onboarding a seed account for the Orca team (acct 123456789012). They need p5, p4d and g5 capacity in eu-west-5. Can infra start a quota/entitlement request for GPUs + ENIs? Need to land instances by next Tuesday if possible.

QuotaBot: New support case created: #CASE-2026-99871. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=CASE-2026-99871 :white_check_mark:

Shiv Patel: How many of each accelerator and what ENI/vCPU ceilings do they need? Do we have a hard date or is this flexible?

Marta V: Planned numbers: p5.xlarge equivalents (we call them p5) x8, p4d (8x16TB host) x4, g5 (for inference) x20. ENIs: expected peak ~60 across two subnets. vCPU aggregate bump probably will be needed — estimate ~160 vCPU. Target reprovision: 2026-03-24 (soft deadline). Cost note: they'll trial with on-demand for 2 weeks — rough monthly burn if constant: ~= $120k.

Kevin O'Neill: For p5/p4d AWS often requires an entitlement request (not just quota increase). Need a clear business justification + monthly spend estimate. Mention sustained usage and whether it's for training/inference. Also ask AWS to raise per-AZ ENI quotas and the EC2 Accelerator quotas.

Kevin O'Neill: Suggested case body (paste into the AWS console):

```
Account: 123456789012
Region: eu-west-5
Request: Increase EC2 Accelerator quotas for p5, p4d and g5 families and ENI limits.
Justification: Onboarding a Redwood customer proof-of-concept (Orca) requiring dedicated inference and eval workloads. Expected steady-state peak: p5 x8, p4d x4, g5 x20. Estimated monthly spend: ~$120k. We require capacity by 2026-03-24. Please advise on entitlement requirements for p5/p4d and next steps.
```

Anya Liu: Also add the ENI quota codes and VPC network-interface quotas — AWS often blocks because of ENI-per-subnet limits. Run this to check current quotas quickly: `aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-3456ABCD` (replace with correct quota codes) and ping infra-aws if any AZ shows low ENI headroom.

Shiv Patel: If AWS flags entitlement delays, fallback plan: spin some inference into eu-west-3 (already approved) and use cross-region routing with caching. That buys time without blocking the onboarding. Also consider enabling burst nodes in Dedicated pool if customer is okay with a short delay.

Marta V: Thanks — I'm updating the case text now with the numbers and justification. I included subnet IDs and the estimated schedule. Tagging @Shiv and @Anya for review before I submit.

QuotaBot: Case #CASE-2026-99871 status updated to "Pending - AWS reviewing entitlement request". Assigned engineer: aws-entitlement-specialist-2. ETA: 48-72 hours.

Kevin O'Neill: Good. When AWS responds, capture any required security docs (SOC/ISO) or usage patterns they ask for and drop them into the case. If they request an uplift in account-level accelerator entitlement, that can take longer — we'll escalate if needed. :+1:

Marta V: Will do. I'll post updates in this thread once the case moves. Thanks everyone. :seedling:
